$comment: How loud each family of recorded sound plays against a gunshot, in dB under the shot (the converter normalizes every file to about -1 dBFS, so without these numbers a spent case lands as loud as the rifle that ejected it). A rifle is 155-165 dB SPL at the muzzle and a brass case on concrete 60-75 dB SPL at a metre: a game cannot hold 80 dB between two sounds, so the case sits 32 dB under the shot and a dropped magazine 24 dB, which keeps both audible near and below the shot after the mix. choke = how many of the family ring at once, per sound id: a full-auto burst leaves a few cases ringing, not one per round.
